ναυστολέω.definition: fut. E.Supp.474: pf; trans., carry or convey by sea, E.Or.741 : metaph., providing matter for their own praise, Pi.N.6.32, cf. Luc.Lex.2:—Pass., with fut. Med. go by sea, E.Tr.1048; Id.Fr.492.6; D.S.4.13

ναυστολία.definition: going by sea, naval expedition, Id.Andr.795 , Str.16.2.23

ναυστολογέω.definition: take as a passenger, metaph. of CIL8.21445

ναυτιάω.definition: mostly in pres. and impf. (aor., Luc.Tox.19; generally, to be disgusted, Demetr.Eloc.15, Phryn.l.c

ναυτικός.definition: of or for a ship, seafaring, naval; of persons, skilled in seamanship, nautical, became a naval power, Th.1.18, cf.7.21; = POxy.929.8

ναυτολογέω.definition: take on board passengers or cargo, PLond.3.1164h19 : metaph., AP9.415

ναυφθορία.definition: shipwreck, loss of ships, AP7.73 : pl., Man.1.324

ναύφθορος.definition: shipwrecked, the garb of shipwrecked men, E.Hel.1382, 1539

νεακόνητος.definition: newly whetted, S.El.1394 ; cf. II fin

νεαλής.definition: newly caught, Suid., Hsch; fresh, not tired, of persons and animals, Ar.Fr.361 ; opp. X.Cyr.8.6.17; Pl.Plt.265b; freq. of soldiers, Plb.3.73.5, cf. 10.14.3; Plu.Ant.39 ; Plu.2.669a; Luc.Merc.Cond.26, cf. Alex.16

νεανεία.definition: spirited, audacious act, Ph.1.258, 2.128, cf. Hdn.Epim.265, Suid.; contr. fr

νεανίας.definition: Ep. and Ion. dat. pl; freq. with the sense of a youth in character, i.e. either in good sense, impetuous, active, E.Ion1041, cf. Ar.V.1333, X.Cyr.1.3.6, D.18.313; or in bad sense, hot-headed, wilful, headstrong, E.Sup…

νεανίευμα.definition: youthful, i.e. spirited or wanton, act or word, Pl.R.390a, Luc.Herm.33, etc.; of an argument, bold attempt, Simp.in Ph.1169.9

νεανιεύομαι.definition: more freq., act like a hot-headed youth, wilfully or wantonly, swagger, Ar.Fr.827, Lys.Fr.324 S.; behave so towards . . , Isoc.20.17, cf. Hyp.Eux.27; Pl.Grg.482c; with youthful insolence, Plu.Cic.1:— Pass., to all his…

νεανισκάρχης.definition: official in charge of ib.1162.8, Delph.3.238, IPE2.440, al. , Supp.Epigr.2.620 , BSA29.23 , Philol.11.293

νεανισκεύομαι.definition: only pres., to be in one's youth, Eup.29, Posidipp.9; X.Cyr.1.2.15, Plu.2.12b

νεανίσκος.definition: Ion. youth, young; my young man, i.e. servant, Luc.Alex.53; perh. also, PCair.Zen.18.6 , Ev.Marc.14.51: pl., dub. sens., PCair.Zen.153

νεαροποιέω.definition: make new, refresh, Plu.2.702c:—in Med; Medic., freshen the edges of an ulcer by removing granulations, Antyll. ap. Orib.44.23.4, Ruf. ap.eund.8.24.48

νεαροπρεπής.definition: possessing youthful charm, metaph., of style, Aristid.Rh.2p.551S.; becoming or natural in youth, Procl.in Alc.pp.23,47 C.; Id.in Cra.p.1 P., cf. Olymp.in Phlb.p.249S

νεάω.definition: plough up, of fallow land, . . Ar.Nu.1117: metaph., Pratin.Lyr.5: abs., Eup.13, Thphr.CP3.20.7: aor. 1 subj. ib.3.20.8:—Pass., land ploughed up, after lying fallow, Hes.Op.462

νεβρίας.definition: dappled like a fawn, Arist.HA565a26, cf. Hsch.s.v

νεβριδόπεπλος.definition: clad in fawnskin, of Dionysus and the Bacchae, AP9.524.14

νεβρίς.definition: gen. E.Ba.136 , E.Ba.24, Thesp.1, E.Ba.249, ib.696:—fawnskin, esp. as the dress of Dionysus and the Bacchae, Il.cc

νεβρισμός.definition: wearing of a Arignote ap. Harp

νεβρόομαι.definition: Pass., to be changed into a fawn, Nonn.D.10.60

νεηγενής.definition: Ion. for new-born, just born, Od.4.336

νεήτομος.definition: cut or castrated when young, AP6.234

νείκη.definition: = Epigr. ap. Paus.5.2.5: personified, = v.l. for in Timo21; prob. in A.Ag.1378, E.Or.1679, Poet. ap. D.Chr.32.82, cf. EM276.3

Νειλοβροχέω.definition: in Pass., to be inundated by the Nile, POxy.1502v.6

Νειλόβροχος.definition: inundated by the Nile , PRyl.208.30 , etc

Νειλοθερής.definition: burnt by the Nile, i. e. by the sun and air of Egypt, A.Supp.71

Νειλομέτριον.definition: Nilometer, a rod graduated to show the rise and fall of the Nile, Str.17.1.48, Hld.9.22, POxy.43 VVI :—Adj. used in the graduation of the Nilometer, ib.669.36

Νειλῷος.definition: = Luc.Nav.15, PMasp.2 ii 21 ; festival on the inundation of the Nile, Hld.9.9

Νειλώτης.definition: in or on the Nile, Ath.7.309a: fem., the land of the Nile, A.Pr.814

νεκραγωγέω.definition: conduct the dead, of Hermes, Id.Cont.2

νεκρεπάρτης.definition: remover of corpses, Cat.Cod.Astr.8.110, 8.215, prob. l. ib.7.117

νεκριμαῖος.definition: = of animals, Aq.De.14.8, Sch.Ar.Av.538, OGI629.158 , Erot. and Hsch. s.v. also of a human being, LXX3 Ki.13.25

νεκροθήκη.definition: coffin or urn, E.Fr.472.17 ; place for a coffin or urn, prob. in Rev.Bibl.39.532

νεκροκομίζω.definition: take care of the dead, Eust.1080.51

νεκροκόσμος.definition: laying corpses out for burial, Plu.2.994e

νεκροπέρνας.definition: one who sells corpses, i. e. Achilles, Lyc.276

νεκρόπολις.definition: city of the dead, a name given to a suburb of Alexandria, Str.17.1.10 and 14

νεκροστολέω.definition: ferry the dead, of Charon, Luc.Cont.24

νεκρόταγος.definition: judge of the dead, of Minos, Lyc.1399

νεκροτάφος.definition: = PRyl.65.3 , Ostr.Bodl. iv 51 , PGrenf.2.73.7 , AJP34.439 , Cat.Cod. Astr.7.117, Man.4.192

νεκροφορέω.definition: bear as a dead body to the burial: metaph., of soul bearing body, Ph.2.540, cf. 1.100

νεκροφόρος.definition: burying corpses, burying the dead, Plu.Cat.Ma.9, Gloss

νεκροφύλαξ.definition: guardian of the dead, Ph.1.417, Vett.Val.68.14, Cat.Cod.Astr.8.139

νεκτάριον.definition: name of a medicine, Gal.13.282; of various eye- salves, Id.12.750,773

νεκυαγωγή.definition: calling up of spirits, necromancy, PMag.Par.1.222

νεκυάμβατος.definition: of Charon's boat, embarked in by the dead, Epic. ap. Paus.10.28.2

νεκυδαίμων.definition: ghost of a dead man, PMag.Par.1.368, al., Tab.Defix.Aud. 234.1

νεκυηπόλος.definition: having to do with the dead, Man.1.330

νεκυοδαίμων.definition: god of the dead, Sammelb.4947 , Rev.Phil.1930.249

νεκυομαντεία.definition: sub-title of Luc.Menipp.; also of the eleventh Book of the Odyssey, Hermog.Prog.2, Eust.1670.23: pl. = defixiones, Gloss

νεκυομαντεῖον.definition: Ion. oracle of the dead, where ghosts were called up, Cic.Tusc.1.16.37, D.S.4.22, Plu.Cim.6, Paus.9.30.6: in pl., PMag.Lond.121.285

νεκυοπομπός.definition: name of a mythical lake, Sch.Od.p.5 Buttm

νεκυοστόλος.definition: ferrying the dead over the Styx, of; bearing the dead, of a bier, AP7.634

Νεμεσεῖον.definition: temple of Nemesis, St.Byz. s.v. Theognost.Can.129; written Bull.Soc.Alex. No.4p.50

νεογηλής.definition: acc. sg. v.l. for in Anacr.51 ap. Sch.Pi.O.3.52; fort. from = sq

νεόδαρτος.definition: newly stripped off, Od.4.437; newly flayed, X.An.4.5.14

νεοδίδακτος.definition: of dramas, poems, etc., newly produced, Luc.Tim.46

νεόδμητος.definition: newly tamed: metaph., of; newly killed, E.Rh.887 , Lyc.65

νεόδρεπτος.definition: fresh-plucked or broken, A.Supp.334, cf. Nic.Th.863 ; wreathed with fresh-plucked leaves, Theoc.26.8

νεοειδής.definition: fresh or youthful in form, Poll.2.10

νεοεργής.definition: just made or newly wrought, Hsch

νεοθηλής.definition: Dor. fresh-budding; of animals, new-born, Anacr.51, AP9.274 , cf. Gal.4.718

νεόθλιπτος.definition: newly pressed or squeezed, Nic.Al.299, cf.Dsc.5.32

νεόθρεπτος.definition: newly grown, A.R.3.1400, prob. in; fresh-curdled, of cheese, Hsch

νεόκμητος.definition: newly wrought, Nic.Th.498; just slain, v.l. for E.Rh.887

νεόκτιστος.definition: also Pi.N.9.2:—newly founded or built, Pi. l.c., P.4.206, Hdt.5.24, Th.3.100, Cic.Att.6.2.3; newly created, LXXWi.11.18:—also B.16.126, Nonn.D.18.294

νεόλεκτος.definition: I.2) newly enlisted, recruit, Nic.Dam.130.31 J., Jul.Or.1.18b, Wilcken Chr.469.3 , Hsch

νεόλυτος.definition: resolved in a new fashion, Lyr.Adesp.112 = Trag.Adesp.136

νεολώφητος.definition: having just left off, Hsch., Phot

νεόνυμφος.definition: newly married, Sostrat. ap. Stob.4.20.70, Supp.Epigr.3.216 , IG12.472 , Plu.2.310e, f.l. for in Suet. Ner.39

νεοπενθής.definition: in new sorrow, fresh-mourning; Pass., lately mourned, IG12.447.6 , cf. 14.1663

νεοπευθής.definition: late-learnt, prob. for Hsch., for Phot

νεοπηγής.definition: lately built or made, AP9.808 ; Orac. ap. Eus.PE4.9:—also fresh-curdled, Batr.38; newly burnt, Hp.Mul.2.206; newly built, Hld.6.11

νεόπλουτος.definition: newly become rich, opp. : hence, vainglorious, upstart, D.17.23, cf. Arg.D.17, Arist.Rh.1387a23; Luc.Hist.Conscr.20; Plu.2.634c; Id.Luc.40: hence, by a comic metaph., of a low upstart, Ar.V.1309

νεόπλυτος.definition: newly washen, Od.6.64, cf. Hdt.2.37, Mus.Belg.16.71 , v.l. in Anacr.21.6

νεοποιός.definition: one who ploughs up fallow land, Poll.1.221

νεόπτολις.definition: poet. for new- founded city, A.Eu.687

νεοπτορθής.definition: with new branches, Hdn.Gr.1.79:—also as etym

νεοπυρίητος.definition: just come out of a vapour-bath, Hp.Superf.29, Nat.Mul.6

νεόρραντος.definition: newly sprinkled, a fresh-reeking sword, S.Aj.30, 828; newly shed, Aristid.Or.24 . 44

νεορρύφητος.definition: having lately taken liquid nourishment, Hp.Acut.65

νεοσίγαλος.definition: new and sparkling, with all the gloss on, metaph., Pi.O.3.4

νεόσμηκτος.definition: newly cleaned, Il.13.342; Euph.132; AP6.227 ; Plu.Aem.32

νεοσπαδής.definition: = newly drawn from a wound, bloody, A.Eu.42

νεοσπάς.definition: newly torn away, fresh-plucked, S.Ant.1201, cf. Fr.502

νεόσπειστος.definition: newly poured as an offering, f.l. in Nonn.D.19.177

νεοσσεύω.definition: Att. Ion. and Hellenistic; build a nest, Arist.HA559a4, etc.; J.AJ5.8.6: metaph., LXXSi.1.15:—Pass., as many as had their nests, Hdt.1.159

νεοσσίς.definition: name of a kind of shoe, Herod.7.57

νεοσσοποιέω.definition: later = LXXIs.13.22:—also in Med., Aesop.5: metaph., Longin.44.7

νεοσσοτροφέω.definition: Att. later rear young birds, AP9.346 : —Pass., to be reared as in the nest, of a child, Ar.Nu.999, cf. Ph.2.200

νεοσύλλογος.definition: newly collected, i.e. incurred, Hyp.Ath.11; newly levied, Plb.3.70.10, cf. Polyaen.3.11.8

νεοσύστατος.definition: recently formed, i.e. recent, of; having newly joined a sect, proselyte, J.BJ2.8.9

νεοτελής.definition: newly initiated, Pl.Phdr.250e , Luc.DMeretr.11.2; Him.Or.14.12; Id.Ed.10.6

νεοτερπής.definition: new and charming, Opp.H.3.352, etc.: neut. as Adv., with new delight, Id.C.2.584

νεότμητος.definition: Dor. newly cut off, divided, Pl.Ti.80d, Theoc.7.134, A.R.3.857, Dsc.2.70

νεότοκος.definition: new-born: metaph., fresh, recent; parox. Act., having just brought forth, E.Ba.701, Aret.CA2.3; D.H.1.79, Plu.2.320d

νεότομος.definition: fresh-cut, A.Ch.25; freshly cut off, E.Ba.1170

νεότρωτος.definition: lately wounded or hurt, Hp.Fract.28; fresh sores, Id.Liqu.4, Dsc.4.114 , cf. Gal.10.257

νεουργέω.definition: invent new things, f.l. in Alciphr.3.51

νεουργός.definition: new-made, new, Pl.R.495e; Plu.Aem.18; shipbuilder, Poll.1.84

νεόφθαρτος.definition: newly ruined or killed, Hsch. s.v

νεοχμέω.definition: = in Pass., Procop.Arc.30 codd., Suid. s.v

νεόχμωσις.definition: innovation, Hsch.: in pl., strange; renovation, Aret.CA2.3; renewal, ib.1.10

νεόω.definition: renovate, change, A.Supp.534; = Poll.1.221: c. acc. cogn., LXXJe.4.3

νευρεπέντατος.definition: stretched on the bowstring, prob. in Tim.Pers.31

νευρίον.definition: Dim. of Hp.Mochl.1, Gal.2.400; Dim. of AP11.352.11

νευροβάτης.definition: rope-dancer, Rhetor.inCat.Cod.Astr.8.213, Et.Gud.345.52: in Lat. form, Vopisc.Carin.19, Firm.Math.8.17.4

νευρόθλαστος.definition: bruised in the sinews, Gal.13.576, Orib.Fr.88

νευροκοπέω.definition: hamstring, hough, LXXGe.49.6, PCair.Zen.462.4 , Plb.31.2.11, Str.16.4.10:—Pass., D.S.3.26

νευροραφέω.definition: or stitch or mend shoes, Pl.Euthd.294b, X.Cyr.8.2.5

νευρορράφος.definition: one who makes strings for the lyre, Lycurg.Fr.100

νευροσπαδής.definition: drawn by the string, the arrow drawn and just ready to fly, S.Ph.290

νευροσπαστέω.definition: put in motion by strings, of puppets; Pass., to be caught by drawing a string, of birds, Ath.9.391a

νευροσπαστία.definition: motion by means of strings, metaph., M.Ant.6.28, 7.29

νευρόσπαστος.definition: drawn by strings, puppets moved by strings, Hdt.2.48; puppets, X.Smp.4.55, Luc.Syr.D.16, etc

νευροστρόφος.definition: tightener of the strings of a musical instrument, Porph.Gaur.12.1

νευροτενής.definition: stretched by sinews, a snare of gut, AP6.109

νευροτομέω.definition: cut the sinews, Agathin. ap. Orib.10.7.9

νευρότονον.definition: strand of gut in a torsion-engine, f.l. in HeroBel.83.4

νευρότρωτος.definition: wounded in the sinews or tendons, Dsc.1.58, Androm. ap. Gal.13.419, Gal.13.563, Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.50

νευροχαρής.definition: delighting in the bowstring or in the lyre, epith. of Apollo, AP9.525.14

νεφεληγερέτα.definition: Ep. for used by Hom. only in nom. and in gen. cloud-gatherer, of Zeus, Il.1.511, al.; acc., Emp.149

νεφελίζω.definition: wrap in clouds, in Pass., Sch.Il.15.153

νεφέλιον.definition: Dim. of Arist.Mete.367b9; Astron., nebula, Ptol.Alm.7.5, al., Vett. Val.110.12

νεφελοειδής.definition: cloud-like, of nebulae or star-clusters, Gem.3.4, Ptol.Tetr.149; Hipparch.2.5.15; also of urine, cloudy, Hp.Acut.17

Νεφελοκένταυρος.definition: cloud-centaur, Luc.VH1.16: partly as sprung from Ixion and the cloud, partly as a fantastic shape such as the clouds assume

Νεφελοκοκκυγία.definition: Cloudcuckoo-town, built by the birds in Ar.Av.819, al., a satire on Athens

νεφελόομαι.definition: Pass., to be clouded over, Eust.127.21

νεφόομαι.definition: Pass., to be clouded over, Nic.Dam.68 J., Ph.2.21, Adam.Vent.35, Porph.Antr.27: metaph., Man.4.518

νεφρίτης.definition: fem. = i.e. the first vertebra of the sacrum, Poll.2.179; Th.7.15; Hp.Int.15: also as Subst. , Id.Coac.502: in pl., Id.Aph.3.31, Dsc.1.14

νεφρός.definition: in pl., kidneys, Diog.Apoll.6, Hp.Aph.4.78, Pl.Ti.91a, etc.: in dual, Ar.Ra.475: rarely in sg., Id.Lys.962, Euphro1.25: euphem. for Philippid.5.4: metaph., LXXPs.15.7

νεωκορία.definition: Ion. office of a Ph.1.695, Plu.2.351e, IG14.1026, Man.4.430 : written in IGRom.3.584

νεωκόρος.definition: Dor. GDI 2116.14, al. (Delph; sacristan, Herod.4.41,45, Paus.10.12.5; in a list of silver articles, IG7.3498.25

νεωλκέω.definition: haul a ship up on land, Thphr.HP5.7.2, Plb.1.29.3; D.S.20.47: abs., Aristonym. ap. Stob.4.33.29:—Pass., Ath.8.350b, cf. Alciphr.1.1: metaph., of a corpse, Phld.Mort.28

νεωλκία.definition: hauling up a ship into dock, Aen.Tact.17.1, Arist.Ph.253b18, Thphr.HP5.7.2 , IG22.1028.37 : metaph., Plu.2.136a

νεώλκιον.definition: dry dock, in pl., App.BC5.100, Hsch.s.v

νεωλκός.definition: one who hauls up a ship into dock, Arist.Ph.250a18, SIG1000.22 , Poll.7.190, 10.148

νεωποιέω.definition: serve as Poll.1.11, Supp.Epigr.1.371 :—also OGI485.8 , Ephes.2 No.47: Dor. SIG241.6 , IG7.3073.6

νεωποίης.definition: official in charge of the temple- fabric, SIG46.6 , cf. 353.1 , etc.:— also Inscr.Prien.195.4 , 174.31 ; Supp.Epigr.1.395 , Ephes.2 No.83: Dor. SIG 1023.33, al. ; IGRom.4.1097, 1098, SIG793

νεωποιός.definition: = IG22.1678b A14:— Dor; building ships, Poll.1.84

νεωρέω.definition: to be overseer of a dockyard, Eust.1562.37, Hsch., Phot

νεώριον.definition: dockyard, IG12.57.53, al., Ar.Ach.918, Th.2.93, 3.74, etc.: in pl., E.Hel.1530, Ar.Av.1540, Th.3.92, Lys.12.99, 13.46, Pl.Criti.115c, etc

νεωρός.definition: superintendent of a dockyard, Hsch.: pl., IG12.74.11

νεωτερίζω.definition: Att.fut. Th.4.51: :—make; freq. with an implication of violence, use forcible measures, Id.1.58; Id.4.51; Id.2.3, cf. X.HG2.1.5, D.23.133; Isoc.Ep.7.9:—also in Med., take the law into one's own hands, POxy. 237 vi3

νεωτερισμός.definition: attempt to change; esp. in bad sense; generally, change, as of diet, Sabin. ap. Gal.17.562

νεωτεροποιία.definition: revolutionary spirit, Th.1.102; revolution, Nic.Dam.130.20 J., J.AJ14.15.6, al

νήθω.definition: spin, Cratin.96, Pl.Plt.289c, LXXEx.35.25, AP11.110 , Corn.ND13, Gal.UP1.3 : Ion. impf. AP14.134. , as from

νηκηδής.definition: careless, f.l. in Epic. ap. Pl.Smp.197c

νήκουστος.definition: deaf, not hearing; unheard, unknown, Arat.173

νηλεόθυμος.definition: of ruthless spirit, IG3.1326, BKT5.87; IG14.1648, cf. 2012

νηλεόποινος.definition: punishing ruthlessly, epith. of the Hes.Th.217

νηλίπους.definition: gen. unshod, barefooted, S.OC349 codd., cf. Max. Tyr.30.6: A.R.3.646, Lyc.635, prob. l. for in Lyd.Mag.1.42; cf

νημέρτεια.definition: truth; Dor. used by S.Tr.173 in trim

νημερτής.definition: Dor. , unerring, infallible, of Proteus, Od.4.349, etc.; of Nereus, Hes.Th.235; a sure decree, i.e. one that will infallibly be put in force, Od.1.86,5.30; or to speak sure truths, 3.19, Il.6.376; 3.204; A.l.c. ; A.R.…

νηνεμία.definition: Ion. stillness in the air, calm, in a calm, Il.5.523; there was a calm, a ceasing of all winds , Od.5.392, 12.169; Hdt.7.218; ib.188; opp. Pl.Phd.77e; in calm weather, Arat.1033, A.R.3.970: in pl., Pl.Tht.153c; Timo64…

νήνεμος.definition: without wind, calm; metaph., E.Hec.533; Plu.2.589d

νηοπορέω.definition: poet. for go by sea, AP7.675

νηπελέω.definition: to be powerless, Hp. ap. Gal.19.124: hence restored in Id.Mul.2.113; cf

νηπιάζω.definition: to be as a babe, childish, Erinn.in PSI9.1090.55 + 15 , Hp.Ep.17, 1 Ep.Cor.14.20, Porph.Gaur.12.4

νηπίαχος.definition: Ep. Dim. of childish, infantine, Il.2.338, 6.408, 16.262, Lyr.Alex.Adesp.36.13 ); BionFr.7.2; Opp.H.5.403; of animals, Id.C.1.444, al.: as Subst. child, IG12.445 , Opp.C.3.211

νηπιέη.definition: Ep. form for childhood, childishness, Il.9.491: in pl., Od.1.297; . . in childish fashion, Il.15.363; led them in his folly, Od.24.469

νηπιότης.definition: childhood, infancy; childishness, Pl.Lg.808e, J.AJ1.19.3, 2.9.7; Luc.Halc.3

νήπτης.definition: sober, discreet, Plb.10.3.1, D.S.30.3, 33.21a, Onos.1.1, Ptol.Tetr.160

νηπύτιος.definition: Ep. Dim. of little child; as Adj., childish, Il.20.211; foolish, Orph.L.6

Νήρειος.definition: Adj. of Nereus, i.e; = Ps.-Dsc.3.73:—also ibid

νησιαρχέω.definition: to be governor of an island or group of islands, CIG3655.7

νησιάρχης.definition: governor of an island or islands, Antiph.190.14, Plu.2.823d

νησίαρχος.definition: = foreg., IG11.559 , 1126 , Inscr.Délos 442 B71 ; of Tiberius at Capreae, D.C.58.5

νησίδιον.definition: Dim. of islet, Th.6.2, Arist.Mir.832a24, Str.2.5.30

νησίτης.definition: of, from, or belonging to an island, St.Byz.:—Dor. fem. PEleph.20.48 ; AP7.2

νωθής.definition: sluggish, slothful, Il.11.559; of the understanding, dull, stupid, Hdt.3.53; Hp.Ep.17, cf. A.Pr.62, Pl.Plt.310e

νωθρεία.definition: sluggishness, torpor, indolence, Erot. s.v. Aristid.Quint.2.3, v.l. in Poll.3.122

νωθρεύω.definition: to be sluggish or torpid, Poll.1.159; to be poorly, indisposed, PGiss.17.6 :—Med., PSI6.717.5

νωθρότης.definition: = Hp.Prorrh.1.13,70, Arist.Rh.1390b30; LXX3 Ma.4.5: pl., Gal.8.161

νωπέομαι.definition: to be downcast, Ion Hist.1, Phot. s.v. )

νωταγωγέω.definition: carry on the back, Clearch. ap. Ath.6.258b

νωτιδανός.definition: a kind of I, Arist.Fr.310; called by Epaenet. ap. Ath.7.294d

νωτόγραπτος.definition: having markings on the back, Arist.Fr.297, Eust.1960.20

νωτοκοπέω.definition: break an animal's back, slaughter it, Thd. Ex.13.13, Is.66.3

νωτοφορέω.definition: carry on the back, D.S.2.54: abs., Id.17.105, Vett. Val.77.14

νωτοφόρος.definition: carrying on the back; Subst. carrier, porter, PPetr.3p.139 , LXX2 Ch.34.13, PTeb.115.7

νωχελεύομαι.definition: to be slothful, Aq.Pr.18.9, al. ; malinger, dub. in BGU380.11

νωχελία.definition: Ep. laziness, sluggishness, Il.19.411, cf. Orph.Fr.286, Vett.Val.2.6 , Iamb.VP15.65:—also Orib.Fr.58, Hsch

ναί.definition: Adv., used to express strong affirmation, yea; in answers, yes, Answ. A.Pers.738 , cf. S.El.845 , Pl.Tht.193a, Grg.448b, etc.; doubled, Ar.Nu.1468, Call.Fr.1.56 P., Ev.Matt.5.37

νειόθεν.definition: Ion. Adv. from the bottom, he heaved a sigh from the bottom of his heart, Il.10.10; A.R.1.1197: c. gen., Arat.234; Cerc.4.55; Epic.in Arch.Pap.7.10:—also . . Supp.Epigr.4.467.25 ; in late Prose, heartily, Luc.Peregr.7…

νειόθι.definition: Ion. Adv. at the bottom; under, beneath, opp. A.R.2.355; in stooping posture, Id.3.706: c. gen., Id.1.63, cf. Arat.89. is rarely elided, as in Nic.Al.520.]

νενομισμένως.definition: Adv. in the established manner, Callistr.Stat.6

νεφεληδόν.definition: Adv. in the manner of clouds, Nonn.D.15.1

νεωστί.definition: Adv. of for lately, just now, Hdt.1.196, 2.15,49, al., S.El.1049, Th.4.108, Pl.Grg.503c, Antiph.58.4, etc

νέωτα.definition: Adv. next year, Semon.1.9; elsewh. only X.Cyr.7.2.13,8.6.15, Thphr.Char.3.4; Philem.82; Thphr.HP9.11.9; Id.CP3.16.2; prob. in Schwyzer323 A 12 ; cf

νηποινεί.definition: Adv. of sq., with impunity, esp. in phrase SIG194.10 , Lex ap.And.1.95, Lex ap.D.23.60, cf. Pl.Lg.874c; X.Hier.3.3

νομάδην.definition: Adv., cited as parallel to Sch.Il.3.213

νομιστί.definition: or Adv. conventionally, opp. Diog.Oen.6, cf. Gal.1.417

νοτόθεν.definition: Adv. from the south, Pl. ap. D.L.3.41, Thphr.Sign.11,21: c. gen., prob.l. in IG12.4.9

νουνεχόντως.definition: Adv. of as if from Adj. , sensibly, Isoc.5.7 , Men.1043

νύκτωρ.definition: Adv., by night, Hes.Op.177, Archil.46, S.Aj.47, Ar.Nu.173, Th.258, Antipho5.26, 44, Lys.1.14, 3.6, Pl.Grg.471b, PHal.1.194 , etc. :—the only Adv. of this form, Hdn.Gr.2.952

νυμφοστολικῶς.definition: Adv.like one escorting a bride, Sch.E.Hec.388

νῦν.definition: Adv. now, both of the present moment, and of the present time generally, mortals of our day, Il.1.272; so in Ion. and Att., men of the present day, Hdt.1.68; Pi.O.1.105, B.5.4, cf. Arist.Metaph.1069a26; Th.1.6; ib.12;…

νυστακτικῶς.definition: Adv. in a drowsy way, Gal.19.91

νωλεμές.definition: Adv. without pause, unceasingly, Il.9.317, 17.385, Od.16.191, etc. ; . . Il.17.413: without 14.58; later, firmly, A.R.2.605:—also Il.13.3; persevere, 5.492; but they were murdered without pause, i.e. one after the oth…
